title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
prompt: Given a binary search tree (BST), find the lowest common ancestor (LCA) of two given nodes in the BST. The lowest common ancestor is defined between two nodes p and q as the lowest node in the tree that has both p and q as descendants (where we allow a node to be a descendant of itself).
hints: Use BST property: if p and q are both less than root, LCA is in left subtree. Both greater -> right subtree.
If one is less and one is greater (or one equals root), then root is the LCA.
Recursive: if p.val < root.val and q.val < root.val, go left. Else if both > root.val, go right. Else return root.
O(h) time, O(1) space with iterative approach.
